title: Industriepolitik
summary_en: Industrial policy is back in fashion across the OECD — but its history goes much further back. Juhász and Steinwender contribute this German-language essay to *Aus Politik und Zeitgeschichte* arguing that industrial policy played a foundational role already in the Industrial Revolution, well before the post-1945 German-Japanese-Korean episodes that dominate textbook treatments. They draw on recent quantitative-historical research to document specific Industrial-Revolution-era policy interventions and their measurable impact on industrial development.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for German and EU industrial-policy debates and indirectly for Hungarian industrial strategy (ITM, HIPA): the historical case strengthens the analytical legitimacy of active industrial-policy interventions — currently being expanded under the EU Net-Zero Industry Act and the German Sondervermögen — by showing such tools have a long track record. For Hungary as a manufacturing hub deeply embedded in German supply chains, the paper's argument matters for how the Hungarian policy mix complements EU-level industrial-policy moves.
